analysis.title: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Credibility. NDX Breaks Out. CCC spreads 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: Nasdaq has taken out its highs. Optical names are leading in Japan and TSMC keeps grinding higher. Underneath the index, the median corporate is weaker as higher rates increasingly hurt SMEs and consumers.

The rates curve has steepened considerably, which Privorotsky sees as a healthier configuration than outright front end stress. Front end call skew is bid and back end skew is the reverse. Buying front end rally optionality hedges a growth shock or the Fed backing away from hikes.
Higher long rates hurt parts of the economy, but as long as volatility calms they should not by themselves derail the growth backdrop or core spending.

AI capital race is not slowing, per the DeepSeek fundraising. Compute pricing remains robust and the market is short compute, gigawatts and power infrastructure. Supply is increasingly constrained by politics, so economics must incentivize capacity in harder jurisdictions. Privorotsky finds it hard to be bearish the things that make compute.

Le Pen presents the RN shadow budget on 6 Oct. OATs have already moved a lot for an election still months away, so the bar for a positive surprise is low. Credibility is the realistic upside: more than EUR 25bn a year of identified domestic spending cuts, less reliance on Brussels/immigration savings, slower tax cut phasing, conservative growth assumptions and a binding fiscal rule. Tactically he likes a positive surprise in European banks, French risk and OATs.

Oil: no real breakthrough. Vessels remain at risk and Saudi Arabia is acting more aggressively against the Houthis around Bab el-Mandeb. Both sides look dug in. Enough barrels are moving that Washington's urgency to compromise is lower, particularly near the midterms. The tail risk is escalation against energy infrastructure or asymmetric action. Privorotsky is optimistic but sees the catalyst path as murky.

Risk view: AI is the cleanest part of the setup, with inference demand more durable than appreciated and B200/H200 pricing showing the compute shortage in real time. Rates are calming in the front end and energy has stopped impulsing higher. He sees upside asymmetry for the rest of the low-breadth market into earnings, since nominal growth can still let EPS surprise positively. The risk is that macro looks bad while micro stays strong and the rally broadens.
